caption: The drawing consists of a formal garden plan rendered in shades of green, pink, red, and brown with botanical elements prominently depicted. The composition is divided into two main sections: at the top, an inset illustration shows a neoclassical greenhouse with a central domed entry, flanked by glasshouses and surrounded by lush green lawns, trees, and circular flowerbeds outlined in red and pink; this inset is labeled "THE ELGIN BOTANICAL GARDENS, NEW YORK 1801." Below the inset, the main portion presents a symmetrical garden layout with curving tan-colored paths forming a geometric design on a green lawn. At the center is a large circular flowerbed with various plants and a dense floral arrangement in orange, pink, and green hues; two smaller circular beds containing cacti with pink flowers lie horizontally on either side. Flanking the main garden design at the bottom are detailed botanical illustrations: on the left, purple flowers with green leaves, and large green leaves with conspicuous red veins; in the center, an agave plant with blue-green pointed leaves; on the right, several cacti with pink flowers, palm-like green leaves, and more flowering plants in red, orange, and pink tones. The overall palette is dominated by natural greens, accentuated by vibrant pinks, reds, yellows, and browns.
title: Elgin Botanical Gardens
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
